acceptance: For every result in the deployed results.duckdb, a plain HTTP GET of its permalink returns 200 and the body contains the result ID and each receipt field listed in the description; the page count equals the result count.
An unknown result ID still returns 404.
Existing #run-receipt links from the summary pages land on the receipt section.
In a browser, the Explorer still opens the same permalink with its interactive view; a screenshot or recorded check is attached to the PR.
No artifact listed under removed_legacy in _project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/contract.py is reintroduced, and the site build, parity and deploy checks pass.
A plain HTTP GET of /results/ returns body text that links to /result-summaries/, so a client without JavaScript is not left at 'Loading'.
On every platform and benchmark summary page fetched without JavaScript, the main table holds only runs whose status is Ranked, and the excluded section's heading and reason come before its table.

No result disappears from a summary: per page, ranked rows plus excluded rows equal the previous row count, and every excluded row keeps its numbers and link; the check is run over every summary page and its output is in the PR.
Page generation runs inside the existing site build and parity check, not in a new job.

description:
Problem: /results/r/<public_result_id> returns HTTP 404 with the Explorer shell, so the page exists only for clients that run JavaScript. Every row in the static summaries under /result-summaries/ links there. Search crawlers, chat assistants and plain HTTP clients therefore cannot read or cite a result, although public_result_id is documented as permanent.

Owner decision (2026-11-12): generate one static page per result at the permalink, returning 200, which the Explorer then enhances.

Each page shows, without JavaScript: benchmark, platform and version, scale factor, phase, run date, headline score and geomean with units, ranking status and its reason, trust label, tuning mode, execution environment, a link to the bundle JSON, a cite line carrying the snapshot hash and date, and the 'Derived from' wording where the benchmark is TPC-derived.

Non-goals: no new JSON index or API; the pages are generated from results.duckdb, which stays the single source of metric truth. No hosting change.

Also in scope (owner decisions, 2026-11-13): (1) every published result gets a page, including results for cloud vendors; (2) on the static summary pages, ranked runs stay in the main table and defective or unranked runs move to their own section with the reason stated above the table, numbers kept; (3) the /results/ index links to the summaries for readers without JavaScript. All of this ships on one feature branch and one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site.
